headline: ICE officer shoots a man in Austin after a traffic stop
summary: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man on Austin's north side Sunday afternoon, after a traffic stop. He is in serious but stable condition. Austin police were not part of it. Mayor Kirk Watson wants his own police on the investigation as "clear, third-party eyes." Homeland Security did not respond.
cover_answer: Not settled. Austin's mayor wants his own police on it.
table_question: Should you ever get to referee your own game?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: An officer who works for the government shot a man in Austin, Texas, after his car was pulled over. The man is in the hospital and the doctors have him steady. It happened on one street in one city. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if it comes up. One street, one man, doctors. A five-year-old reads your face first, so the calm is the message and the details are the smallest true ones.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old reads a parent's face before the words, so this script is only for a child who has already heard. It shrinks the event to one street, one man and a hospital. Cantor found the picture frightens this age, not the politics, so the picture is a hospital bed. Expect “will he die?” The chief said serious but stable.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: An ICE officer shot and wounded a man in Austin on Sunday after a traffic stop. ICE works for the national government, so city police weren't part of it. The mayor wants city police on the investigation anyway, like a second referee checking the call: ICE shouldn't judge its own shooting.
8-12.why: A fairness call with a referee in it. This age argues fairness for sport.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether adults apply them to themselves, and this story is that question with a badge on it. The script gives them the chain: federal officer, city police left out, mayor asks in. The second referee is the mechanism. Expect “what did the man do?” We don't know, and the chief said as much.

13-17.script: Who should investigate a shooting when the shooter works for the government? An ICE officer shot a man in Austin on Sunday; the mayor wants city police on the case as "third-party eyes." He also hopes the agent stays in the state. Should that be a hope, or a rule?
13-17.why: Two real questions and no verdict. Let them pick hope or rule first.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two things at once: that the officer may have had cause, and that an agency shouldn't grade its own work. The script hands them both, then hope versus rule. Kuhn's point: argument is practised, and it needs a fair partner. Expect “was he here illegally?” The chief didn't know his nationality. Say so.

5-7.q: Is the man going to be okay?
5-7.a: The police chief said he is hurt but stable, which means the doctors have him steady. We don't know his name.

8-12.q: Why weren't the Austin police there?
8-12.a: ICE is federal, not city. The chief said her officers weren't part of the stop.

8-12.q: Why does the mayor want his police in?
8-12.a: He says the city needs its own eyes on it. ICE shouldn't investigate itself.

13-17.a: Not settled. The mayor wants Austin police in. DHS hasn't answered.
Yes. AP counts ICE shootings in Houston and Maine in July, one fatal.
